title: Closing the parent's first open question
content: The grandparent entry pell-equation-oq-01-oq-04 proved the Pell norm x+y√d is multiplicative (Brahmagupta) and the regulator scales linearly along non-negative powers, R(aⁿ) = n·R(a) for n ∈ ℕ. Its first listed open question asked to extend this to integer (zpow) exponents using the conjugate identity. This file does exactly that: the solution group has inverses, so a solution can be raised to any n ∈ ℤ, and both the norm law pellNorm(aⁿ) = (pellNorm a)ⁿ and the regulator law R(aⁿ) = n·R(a) persist over all of ℤ.
mathContext: $\text{Solution}_1\,d$ is a group; $\;R(a^n) = n\,R(a)$ for every $n \in \mathbb{Z}$.

title: The conjugate identity becomes reciprocation
content: pellNorm_inv turns the parent's conjugate identity pellNorm(a)·pellNorm(a⁻¹) = 1 into pellNorm(a⁻¹) = (pellNorm a)⁻¹ using non-vanishing of the norm. This is the single new ingredient that lets the inductive scaling law cross from positive into negative exponents — the norm of the inverse solution is the multiplicative inverse of the norm.

title: Integer induction across zero
content: pellNorm_zpow is proved by Int.induction_on. The base case is pellNorm(a⁰) = 1. The forward step rewrites a^(n+1) = aⁿ·a, applies pellNorm_mul (Brahmagupta), and closes on the real side with zpow_add_one₀. The backward step rewrites a^(n−1) = aⁿ·a⁻¹, applies pellNorm_mul and pellNorm_inv, and closes with zpow_sub_one₀. The group's zpow steps and the field's zpow steps have identical shapes, so multiplicativity transfers each step with no leftover arithmetic.

title: The regulator is ℤ-linear in the exponent
content: Taking logs of pellNorm_zpow and applying Real.log_zpow (which is unconditional) gives pellRegulator_zpow: R(aⁿ) = n·R(a) for all n ∈ ℤ. The n = −1 instance is pellRegulator_inv (R(a⁻¹) = −R(a)), and pellRegulator_zpow_neg records R(a⁻ⁿ) = −n·R(a). The regulator is therefore a genuine homomorphism (Solution₁ d, ·) → (ℝ, +) on the cyclic subgroup generated by a, with image R(a)·ℤ.
